learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Knowledge and capabilities for the application of materials engineering.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Evaluate, critically and constructively, the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem.
Solve complex problems, autonomously, within the discipline.
Extract conclusions from practical or experimental work and research carried out autonomously.

syllabus_topics: Trends in S-N curves and estimations
Influence of mean stresses in uniaxial fatigue
Combined effects of notches and mean stresses
teaching_methods: Individual study (preparation of readings, exams, elaboration of exercises, class preparation)

assessment_methods.method: Resolution and co-evaluation of individual exercises and group problems

assessment_rules: Written tests, including problems and/or multiple-choice questions, will deduct 1/3 of the value for incorrect answers in the test part. A minimum average score of 4 in the written tests is required to average with exercises/reports/practices and the Integrated Project. The final grade is obtained by weighting written tests (60%), practice reports/problems (15%), and the Integrated Project (25%). For students exempt from the Integrated Project, written tests will account for 75% of the grade, maintaining the same weighting ratio with practice reports/problems. The course is considered passed if the final grade is 5 or higher and no individual component's score is below 4. Students have two annual opportunities to take the written exam.
